profile.headline: Embedded Software Engineer

positions.title: Principal Software Design Engineer, Portland Research and Development Center
positions.description:
The whole group worked for the development of advanced broadcast audio/video/control systems for Marshall Electronics.I mainly worked on developing embedded software from Web UI, device drivers, to applications running on multiple platforms and developing Windows application software. 

We used SourceForge for project management and SVN for software revision control. 

Experienced with MS Visual Studio C/C++, Linux(Ubuntu, Debian, OpenSUSE), embedded Linux like uCLinux, IAR Workbench and μC/OS-II RTOS, Keil MDK and RTX, ARM7 and ARM9, JavaScript, HTML, CGI, U-boot, drivers for devices as like audio, video, FPGA, Dolby modules, and flash memory using SPI/I2C/UART interfaces written in C/C++, and applications written in C using File System, USB, and Network.

These are the products or projects that I have worked on: 
- New Video IP solution: Added IP Camera and Joystick connectivity to this TI DaVinci based audio/video codec system. 
- Audio monitoring system operating uCLInux OS on Analog Device bf548 DSP processor.
- Windows application to calibrate LCD using Klein K-10 and Minolta CA-310.
- Added the network capabilities including Web UI and USB for the monitors operating Keil's RTX OS running on LPC2458 ARM7 processor.
- A Network system to control the monitors through Web UI and several RS485 interfaces based on multiple Linux based platforms as like Intel's ITX board, LPC3250 ARDM9 based phytec board, and Techsol's ARM9 board. 
- A highly integrated display system for remote broadcast trucks using μC/OS-II RTOS and Keil's RTX OS, different IDEs as like IAR's Workbench and Keil's MDX, and different ARM7 processors and Pixelworks' image processors.

positions.title: Principle Application Engineer/Manager of Application Engineering
positions.description:
- Demonstrated an initial product to Taiwan and Korean customers,  got the company's first customer in Korea, managed the project to coordinate the training and the schematic/layout reviews, and helped S/W team to be able to pack/deliver/train SDK to the customers, also helped to debug the customer's system.
- Managed the customer support group mainly making the technical support and document of S/W, OSD, IC, and systems and setting up the trainings for customers and FAEs. Enuclia IC was a Digital TV chip which including MIPS core, MPEG decoder, and 2D graphic engine for OSD, and the scaler. S/W was based on Linux environment by using C++ object oriented architecture.

positions.title: Senior Application Engineer
positions.description:
Oct. 2005 ~ Jul. 2006
Senior System Engineer
Worked with s/w group to develop DCR(Digital Cable Ready) stack for a customer's ATSC/DCR project and got CableLab certification.

Nov. 2003 ~ Oct. 2005
Senior Application Engineer
Worked for Dell+HUMAX’s 32” and 37” ATSC/Hospitality DTV models.
Worked for Dell+LiTong’s 26” analog LCD TV project.
Worked for Sharp+Amtran’s 17” 15” analog LCD TV project.
Dedicated DTV support engineer.
Partially worked for s/w group and system group: 
- Work with S/W group to help a production reference board working with new s/w architecture.
- Work with System’s group to help developing s/w of their AV interface board for tuning the video quality.  

Aug. 2002 ~ Nov. 2003
Senior Product Support Engineer
Design support Pixelworks’ PW181/PW465, turbo 186 compatible, embedded new scale chip, for 23”, 30” and 17” LCD TV and projector application of LG, which was Pixelworks’ Alpha customer of PW181/PW465 chips.
Worldwide Customer support Pixelworks’ Deinterlacer chips as like PW1230/PW1231/PW1225/PW1225 for Japan/Europe/Korea/China/Taiwan customers. 

Apr. 2001 ~ Aug. 2002
Senior Cooperate Support Engineer for Korea
Design support Pixelworks’ all products, 8086 embedded scale chip, for all Korean customers.
Design support Pixelworks’ PW113/PW114, 8086 embedded scale chip, for the smart panel projects of Samsung AMLCD.


Nov.  2000 ~  Apr. 2001
Pixelworks Korea  	Seoul
FAE Manager
[Pixelworks Field application engineer for Samsung]
Design support Pixelworks’ PW364A, PW264A products, 8086 embedded scale chip, at LCD monitor, projector, PDP, and projection TV applications in Samsung in Korea.

positions.description: [Dedicated engineer for Pixelworks’ image scale chip]

positions.title: Senior Application Engineer
positions.description: [Dedicated engineer for NS’s whole PC and micro-controller product, DSP processor, and Fax Engine product]

positions.title: Manager of software dept.
positions.description:
Apr. 1994 ~ Aug. 1996
Manager of software dept.
[Managed whole facsimile software.]
Programmed digital answering function to facsimile machine which exported to British Telecom.
Programmed software of cellular facsimile which was 1st car-facsimile model in Korea.
Programmed 900MHz cordless phone facsimile which was 1st 900MHz Cordless facsimile in Korea and exported to Europe.

Apr. 1990 ~ Apr. 1994
Assistant Manager of facsimile R&D, software dept.
[Provided differentiated facsimile solution to company.]
Designed high-end Multi-Function-Peripheral facsimile functionality with NS’s facsimile engine, NS32FX161 and NS32FX200, in UNIX system.
Designed low-end thermal facsimile functionality with UMC’s facsimile engine, UMC’s 9602 embedded processor.

Apr. 1988 ~ Apr. 1990
Engineer of facsimile R&D, software dept.
[Joined this company when established and developed whole G3 facsimile protocol.]
[Developed more than 3 models of thermal facsimiles, exported to USA and German and contributed the company to be the number one low-end facsimile manufacturer to exceed Samsung.]
By using Intel’s 80188 processor in Assemble and C language
- Programmed facsimile protocol ITU T.4 (MH, MR, and MMR) and T.30.
- Programmed additional facsimile features as like memory, broadcasting, and relay transmission/reception.
Programmed op-panel functions controlling LED, LCD, and keypad of facsimile machine by using Intel’s 8051 in assemble language.
Controlled Rockwell’s facsimile Modem compliant with ITU V.21, V.27, and V.27.
